questions.key_step: Rewrite as 3-(2cos x-1)^2 vs 3/sin x (or bound by 3 sin x); show LHS<=3<RHS.
questions.justification: Needs the sin3x expansion and a bounding comparison rather than direct solving; one non-obvious idea, short chain.

questions.key_step: Reduce cos^4+sin^4 and cos^6+sin^6 to sin^2 2x; get tan^2 2x=1 and count in [0,2pi].
questions.justification: Standard power-reduction identities then a counting step over two periods; routine multi-step.

questions.key_step: Combine sqrt3 sec+cosec into cos(x-60deg)/(sin cos); equate cos(x-60)=cos2x, filter roots in S, sum.
questions.justification: Several identity steps, two root families, exclusion of excluded points and a sum; options help a little.

questions.key_step: Convert to a quadratic in t=tan(x/2) (or R cos(x-phi)) and use tan((a+b)/2) from sum/product of roots.
questions.justification: Standard t-substitution but the symmetry/sum-of-roots step must be spotted; numerical answer with no options.

questions.key_step: Count solutions of four equations in given closed intervals, watching endpoints (II at -5pi/18, III count 6, IV count 4).
questions.justification: Four independent counts with endpoint precision, but options allow elimination.

questions.key_step: Bound sin^6<=sin^2, cos^4<=cos^2 to force equality; reduce others to quadratic in cos x and cos x=0.
questions.justification: Same question as the official 2026-P1-Q14 which the user rated 4: four counts, one needs a bounding idea, one needs rejecting an out-of-range root.
